cohort: The study included 279 cases of vasa previa (VP) from all 408 perinatal centers in Japan.
finding: Vasa previa was diagnosed prenatally in >95% of cases across all types, and a low-lying placenta was less common in Type 1 VP, but no significant differences were found in maternal backgrounds or short-term perinatal outcomes among the three types of VP.
mod_finding: No significant differences were noted in perinatal management, which would include mode of birth, among the three types of VP.
followup_time: Short-term perinatal outcomes (e.g., Apgar score at 5 minutes, umbilical artery pH at birth)
